items.claim: The seven-item enumeration across 6:17-19 answers the six/seven numerical formula opened at 6:16, and both edges of the span are corroborated (not driven) by petuchah marks at 6:15 and 6:19, so the numerical_saying unit and its boundaries hold.
items.evidence: Byte tier confirms the count formula "שֶׁשׁ הֵ֭נָּה... וְ֝שֶׁ֗בַע" opens oshb:Prov.6.16; 6:17-19 enumerate exactly seven objects (eyes, tongue, hands, heart, feet, witness, discord-sower), matching the stated seven; the ketiv/qere pair "תועבות תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת" at 6:16 (pmarks_Prov.json kq) is correctly disclosed as bearing on the noun's number/state, not the count; petuchah marks at Prov.6.15 and Prov.6.19 (pmarks_Prov.json marks, both PE) are confirmed and correctly treated as tier-3 corroboration, never a driver.

items.claim: The row's back boundary at 6:23 mischaracterizes 6:24 as opening independent material naming a fresh threat not yet in view, when the infinitive-of-purpose clause at 6:24 grammatically completes the sentence begun at 6:23 (WEB itself joins them with a comma, not a period) and no petuchah corroborates a seam there.
items.evidence: web:Prov.6.23 ends "...are the way of life," continuing directly into web:Prov.6.24 "to keep you from the immoral woman..." in the very witness this row cites; the Hebrew purpose infinitive "לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת..." (oshb:Prov.6.24) attaches back to the imperative chain of 6:20-23 rather than opening its own clause; pmarks_Prov.json shows no petuchah/setumah at 6:23 (nearest marks are 6:19 before this row and 6:26 inside the next row), so the claimed edge carries zero tier-3 corroboration; the identical construction "לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה..." recurs verse-for-verse at oshb:Prov.7.5, and the same cluster's P04-001 keeps 7:1-23 unified as one instruction_lecture across that identical seam rather than splitting there, an inconsistent, undisclosed application of the same byte-true device (cross-seam cohesion).

items.claim: The rationale frames 6:24's purpose infinitive as governing the whole span from a fresh start, but the same clause is the grammatical tail of the sentence opened at 6:23 (WEB's own comma, not a period, joins them), so this row's front boundary overstates 6:24's independence.
items.evidence: web:Prov.6.23-24 reads as one continuous sentence in the cited witness itself; oshb:Prov.6.24 "לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת..." matches oshb:Prov.7.5 "לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה..." construction-for-construction (the identical infinitive-of-purpose to-keep-you-from opener), yet this same cluster's P04-001 keeps 7:1-23 as a single instruction_lecture across that identical seam; pmarks_Prov.json has no petuchah/setumah at the claimed 6:23/6:24 edge (the only nearby marks, 6:19 before and 6:26 inside this row's own span, are already disclosed as non-drivers), so the front-boundary claim rests on a mischaracterization of the purpose clause's syntax, not on independent byte evidence.

items.claim: Two of the row's WEB citations break the mandatory curly-quote-with-inline-ref convention by rendering verbatim WEB text in straight quotes, and one of those, will-not-spare-in-the-day-of-vengeance, does not match the cited witness's actual wording.
items.evidence: The rationale field quotes "is void of understanding" and "will not spare in the day of vengeance" in straight quotes while citing web:Prov.6.32 and web:Prov.6.34-35 as source, inconsistent with the curly-quote convention used elsewhere in the very same field for "destroys his own soul" and "won't regard any ransom"; web:Prov.6.34 text is "For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband. He won't spare in the day of vengeance." -- the row's quoted string "will not spare" is not byte-verbatim to the source's contraction "won't spare," a quote-fidelity defect distinct from mere quote-mark style.

items.claim: The 7:1-23 span is well-bounded: the vocative restart at 7:1 follows the petuchah closing 6:35, the purpose clause of 7:5 is grammatically continued by the causal particle opening 7:6 into the window-scene report, and the span closes at the petuchah of 7:23 before plural address resumes at 7:24.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.7.1 verse-initial "בְּ֭נִי" is confirmed against the bni-vocative inventory's chs.1-7 spine; pmarks_Prov.json confirms petuchah at Prov.6.35 and Prov.7.23 (both PE) with no petuchah between them, consistent with keeping the report unified; the causal particle opening oshb:Prov.7.6 and the scene-turn particle opening oshb:Prov.7.10 are both byte-confirmed; the paseq at Prov.7.12 (pmarks_Prov.json paseq) is correctly disclosed as a bare count entry, not a positional claim.

items.claim: The 7:24-27 span is a well-corroborated closing bracket: the plural address at 7:24 echoes the singular vocative that opened the lecture at 7:1, the inset narrative closes at the petuchah of 7:23 just before this span begins, and the span itself closes at the petuchah of 7:27, the chapter's end.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.7.24 opens "בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ" (plural sons), byte-distinct from but echoing the singular "בְּ֭נִי" of oshb:Prov.7.1; pmarks_Prov.json confirms petuchah at Prov.7.23 and Prov.7.27 (both PE); web:Prov.7.24 and web:Prov.7.27 curly-quoted text matches the cited witness verbatim.

items.claim: The 8:1-21 span holds together as one wisdom_poem: the narrator's third-person setup (8:1-3) has no disclosed parashah seam before wisdom's first-person call begins at 8:4, and the self-commendation opened at 8:12 runs uninterrupted to the petuchah at 8:21 that precedes the Yahweh-subject turn of 8:22.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.8.1 "הֲלֹֽא חָכְמָ֥ה תִקְרָ֑א וּ֝תְבוּנָ֗ה תִּתֵּ֥ן קוֹלָֽהּ" and oshb:Prov.8.12 "אֲֽנִי חָ֭כְמָה" are both byte-confirmed; pmarks_Prov.json shows petuchah at Prov.7.27 (before this span) and Prov.8.21 (at its close) with no petuchah/setumah entry between 8:1 and 8:21, consistent with the row's claim that the parashah layer discloses no internal seam; web:Prov.8.1, web:Prov.8.4, web:Prov.8.11 and web:Prov.8.21 curly quotes match the cited witness verbatim.

items.claim: The 8:22-31 span is well-bounded by a genuine grammatical subject shift to Yahweh at 8:22 immediately after the petuchah closing 8:21, and by the petuchah at 8:31 that precedes the renewed address of 8:32, which repeats the exact refrain of 7:24 verbatim.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.8.22 opens "יְֽהוָ֗ה קָ֭נָנִי" (byte match; Yahweh as grammatical subject, distinct from wisdom's own first-person voice in 8:1-21); pmarks_Prov.json confirms petuchah at Prov.8.21 and Prov.8.31 (both PE) and paseq at Prov.8.29 and Prov.8.30, correctly disclosed as bare count entries; oshb:Prov.8.32 "וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ לִ֑י וְ֝אַשְׁרֵ֗י דְּרָכַ֥י יִשְׁמֹֽרוּ" is byte-identical to oshb:Prov.7.24's opening "וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ לִ֑י", correctly read by the row as the marker that separates this span from the renewed address.
